patterns.usage_note: Joins two or more alternatives one of which is to be settled on (紅茶かコーヒー, 行くか行かないか), so it fits deciding, choosing, and not knowing which one holds. The sibling entry is the sentence-final question marker, which closes a clause and questions the whole proposition (もう終わったか). It attaches to nouns, plain-form verbs, i-adjectives and た, and the last か is often dropped before a particle (お茶かコーヒーを飲む).

examples.ruby: 紅茶[こうちゃ]かコーヒーか、好[す]きな方[ほう]を選[えら]んでください。
examples.english: Tea or coffee — take whichever you prefer.

examples.ruby: 電車[でんしゃ]で来[く]るか歩[ある]いて来[く]るか、決[き]めておいて。
examples.english: Decide in advance whether you're coming by train or on foot.

examples.ruby: 傘[かさ]を電車[でんしゃ]に置[お]いたか店[みせ]に忘[わす]れたか、思[おも]い出[だ]せない。
examples.english: I can't remember whether I left my umbrella on the train or at the shop.
